text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam sponsors a meeting to reconcile Lebanese officials.
- The United Nations studies a bill to fine Israel for shelling a U.N. base in Qana, in south Lebanon, where about 100 civilians taking shelter were killed.
- Security authorities warn the inhabitants of east Lebanon Bekaa valley not to return to cultivating hashish.
- World Bank President James Wolfensohn will make a visit to Lebanon after visiting Syria on Saturday. It will be the first visit by a World Bank president to Lebanon.
- A fourth group of Lebanese nationals in Sierra Leone arrives in Beirut.
- The five-nation group monitoring ceasefire in Lebanon will meet on Sunday to discuss two complaints, one by Lebanon and the other by Israel.
- Khaddam says Syria has no problem with the Christians and any dialogue to take place will be with Lebanese officials only.
- The International Labour Organisation sends a delegate to Lebanon to mediate over the split in Lebanon's Labour Confederation.
- The secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference arrives in Beirut on an official visit.
